claims.claim: A 2007 Center on Education Policy survey found about 62 percent of surveyed districts increased time for reading/language arts and math.
claims.episode_span: A 2007 survey by the Center on Education Policy found that 62 percent of districts had increased time for tested subjects
claims.source_title: Reading, math eat up class hours - The Atlantic Philanthropies (Baltimore Sun reprint on the CEP report)
claims.supporting_quote: about 62 percent of the 349 school systems surveyed reported that they increased time in reading/language arts and math

claims.claim: In the same CEP survey, 44 percent of districts made more time for reading and math by cutting time from other subjects such as social studies and science.
claims.episode_span: while 44 percent had cut time for social studies, science, art, or music
claims.source_title: Reading, math eat up class hours - The Atlantic Philanthropies (Baltimore Sun reprint on the CEP report)
claims.supporting_quote: 44 percent of districts said they created more time for reading and math by reducing time for social studies and science

claims.claim: Analysts documented early in NCLB implementation that districts were already shifting instructional time toward reading and math at other subjects' expense (CEP's 2006 finding, reported as 71 percent of districts).
claims.episode_span: A smaller number of analysts noted that schools were already shifting instructional time away from social studies, science, and the arts
claims.source_title: Reading and Math Gain Ground with Education Law - NPR (March 2006)
claims.supporting_quote: 71 percent of the nation's 15,000 school districts now spend less instructional time on everything else in order to devote more time to reading and math

claims.claim: President George W. Bush signed the No Child Left Behind Act into law on January 8, 2002.
claims.episode_span: President Bush signed it into law on January 8, 2002
claims.source_title: No Child Left Behind Act - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: Signed into law by President George W. Bush on January 8, 2002

claims.claim: NCLB mandated annual reading and math testing in grades 3 through 8 and at least once in high school.
claims.episode_span: Every state had to administer annual reading and mathematics tests in grades 3 through 8 and once in high school
claims.source_title: No Child Left Behind Act - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: a student's progress in reading and math was mandated to be measured annually in grades 3 through 8 and at least once during high school via standardized tests

claims.claim: Schools missing Adequate Yearly Progress for a second consecutive year were labeled 'In Need of Improvement' and entered an escalating sequence of interventions.
claims.episode_span: for two consecutive years faced a sequence of interventions culminating in possible staff replacement
claims.source_title: No Child Left Behind Act - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: Schools that miss AYP for a second consecutive year are publicly labeled as "In Need of Improvement," and must develop a two-year improvement

claims.claim: NCLB required science assessment once in each of three grade spans beginning in the 2007-2008 school year.
claims.episode_span: The statute did include science testing beginning in 2007–2008
claims.source_title: No Child Left Behind Act - Ballotpedia
claims.supporting_quote: Beginning in the 2007-2008 school year, schools were required to assess students in science once during each of those three grade spans

claims.claim: The 2011 Georgia Bureau of Investigation report on Atlanta Public Schools implicated 178 educators in correcting students' test answers.
claims.episode_span: the 2011 Atlanta investigation revealed that dozens of educators had altered answer sheets to protect their schools
claims.source_title: Atlanta Public Schools cheating scandal - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: The investigation implicated 178 educators in correcting answers entered by students

claims.claim: NCLB was coauthored by a bipartisan group including Rep. John Boehner and Sen. Ted Kennedy, and championed by President Bush.
claims.episode_span: a bipartisan coalition that included President George W. Bush, Representative John Boehner, and Senator Edward Kennedy
claims.source_title: No Child Left Behind Act - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: it was coauthored by the representatives John Boehner , George Miller , and the senators Ted Kennedy and Judd Gregg

claims.claim: President Obama signed the Every Student Succeeds Act into law on December 10, 2015.
claims.episode_span: in December 2015 President Obama signed the Every Student Succeeds Act
claims.supporting_quote: the House passed the bill in a 359–64 vote; days later, the Senate passed the bill in an 85–12 vote. [ 5 ] President Obama signed the bill into law on December 10, 2015
